pos.personaBrief: Spain dominated possession (56.6% in the Euro 2012 final, 20 of 21 big-tournament games over 50%) and Pique said the more ball they have, the less danger the opponent creates; Del Bosque called it 'our game'.

pro.personaBrief: Spain built patiently, knocking the ball about until an opening appeared, with a secure Busquets-Alonso pivot; they pressed high and hounded rather than going long, and Cox criticised the lack of directness.

est.personaBrief: Spain concentrated passing in tight areas, Iniesta and Silva moved inside, and a false nine dropped to link play, but with a clear Busquets/Alonso/Xavi shape.

lar.personaBrief: Spain played through a crowded middle and used a strikerless six-man midfield, though Cox and Holding Midfield note they were most threatening with width from Navas, Pedro and Villa when the middle was shut.

blo.personaBrief: Spain pressed superbly and early (Wilson, Holding Midfield, Libertad Digital), with forwards starting the press and a high line, and won the ball back quickly after losing it.

mar.personaBrief: Spain defended with collective cover and zonal-style help (Busquets covering for Arbeloa, no man-marking of Ronaldo), and set-piece marking is not documented.

pla.personaBrief: Del Bosque said they always play with the same idea regardless of the rival, Plan A to live and die by, stubborn through 2012, though he adapted the system to his available players.

res.personaBrief: Spain won 1-0 through the knockouts but insisted on their style, which Del Bosque said gave them everything; he looked for the secure win but through possession, bringing on Torres to stretch rather than closing down.

sis.personaBrief: A collective with stars in defined roles: everyone pressed, and Del Bosque used the same system with fixed duties for Xavi, Iniesta and Villa, though the talent was exceptional.

jog.personaBrief: Spain was built on technique: Xavi, Iniesta, Silva, Busquets and Alonso as the best passing holding duo, with little emphasis on aerial or physical duels.

bas.personaBrief: Del Bosque kept the same veteran core that won in 2008-10 (same XI in opener and final, Puyol valued for experience), bringing in newcomers like Alba gradually.

lid.personaBrief: Del Bosque was understated and tranquil, a man-manager who handled egos with calm and valued dressing-room weight, while still making unsettling calls like dropping Fabregas.
